- Speak to whoever's already stirring—Wren's usually up with the cockerel, Marta needs the ovens
- Head straight for the forest to start early, prove something to himself and maybe to himself alone
- Find Tobias, somehow, to—what? Apologize? That wouldn't come out right

What he knows: he has 1,800 sim. He has no food. His household will be charged upkeep today whether they eat or not, and he's not carrying his share of that burden yet.

He looks at the door, then at the interior of the house. Wren's probably in the field already, or near to. Marta would be at the mill or the ovens. Idris—

Corwin listens to Marta lay it bare—the bakery failing, Bram's cushion gone quiet, the whole house teetering on a week's margin. Five thousand and two hundred sim sounds like a fortune to a man with eighteen hundred, but Marta's right: it won't weather a cold snap and closed books both.

He looks at Idris when Marta asks for someone to walk to the Chestnut. The old man's already said "Forest first, I'll eat later"—typical Idris, work before belly, same as always. But Corwin sees the opening. He could say he'll go with Marta. Help carry flour, hear what she needs to say to Ainsley. Delay the forest work, delay the proof he's been trying to make with every tree he fells faster than his uncle ever did.

Or he could do what Marta's really asking—clear that slope for Wren, get the timber she needs for her field and maybe for sale besides. That's the work that feeds the house directly. That's the work that proves something too, but quieter.

He speaks before he can think himself in circles. "I'll clear the slope. Wren needs that ground, and timber's what I've got to give." He glances at Idris, a briefly complicated thing passing between them—Idris who taught him, Idris who told him to leave it about Tobias. "If you're both at the Chestnut, maybe ask Ainsley about Bram's books while you're there. To be fair, closed accounts aren't like him. Something's shifted there."

He wants to say more about Liora—the student with nothing in her pack, same as him—but the words stick. She's got her own path, Marta said. Who is he to chart it?

"Forest by seven, then," he says, and he's already calculating: three hours hard work before he breaks, timber to drag, no food to fuel it. The hunger will come. He's felt it before. </think> A simple acknowledgment to Marta—he's heard the situation, he's taking the work she needs done. He doesn't need to make a speech of it. The Thorne household runs on practical talk.  Three to the Chestnut, me to the forest. The household scatters more thinly than Marta would like, I can see it in her set jaw. But timber clears the slope clears the field clears the debt. It's a chain I can work with my own hands.

I wait to see if anyone speaks before the breaking. Idris is gone already, ghosted out for his own purposes. Liora probably calculating how to slip away without the fieldwork. Wren with her farmer's patience, waiting for the rest of us to clear so she can grow.

I should move. The forest won't walk to me. But I linger one breath more, listening for anything else Marta needs to say plain. </think>   Corwin feels the conversation thinning, the household pulling apart to their separate burdens. He should move—forest by seven, he said, and he keeps his word. But something holds him a moment longer, watching his aunt's face in the dim light, seeing the weight she carries that she's only half-shared.

He turns for the door before he can ask more than he's owed. The slope needs clearing. Wren needs her ground. And timber—timber is something he can give, something earned, something that doesn't require words he hasn't found yet.

He walks toward Kasukabe Forest, the morning chill on his neck, his stomach already starting its empty complaint. Three hours hard work on nothing but will. He's done it before. He'll do it until he doesn't have to anymore. 

The forest waits, indifferent to what he's proving or who he's proving it to. That is its honesty, and he goes to meet it.   The house is behind him now. Corwin walks the early road toward the forest, feeling the hollowness in his belly already, knowing he'll work through it. Timber to clear. A slope to open. Work he can do with his hands that needs no explanation, no words he hasn't earned yet.

He moves through the morning, grateful and chafing at once, as always. The forest rises ahead. The work is waiting. Stop here.

He watches Marta's face, sees the relief there barely masked. Liora getting her loaves, the student cared for. The pattern of the Thorne household—some carried, some carrying, never quite equal but always moving.

The forest rises ahead, indifferent to his reasons. That is its honesty, and he goes to meet it. Every step carrying him away from the house where he is grateful and chafing at once, toward the trees where effort settles something, even if it's not the debt he thinks he's paying.
